atoms.text: This is Bella the Beaver. She is going to show you around some different rivers. Let’s start at the source!

instruction.text: Can you put together the definition of source? Select the sentence parts in the correct order.

feedback.finish: Most river sources can be found quite high up, and the water flows down to other rivers, lakes and even the sea!

instruction.text: This is Pumlumon in Wales. Select the top of the mountain to learn more.
instruction.sound: This is Pum-limmon in Wales. Select the top of the mountain to learn more.

text: A spring is a type of river source where water naturally bubbles up from underground. There are two springs on this mountain.

instruction.text: Now we’re in the Alps. Select the stream to learn more.

feedback.end: When the snow and ice melts, water flows into small streams that join together to form rivers. Rivers can also be started by rainfall.

instruction.text: This is Lake Victoria in Africa. Select the island to learn more.

feedback.end: Lake Victoria is the biggest lake in Africa. It is also the source of the River Nile, which is the longest river in the world!

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Bella would like to find the source of this river. Answer Bella’s questions.

atoms.a: “We are facing upstream, which direction does the compass say the river comes from?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>We are facing upstream, which direction does the compass say the river comes from</voice>

hint.label: Upstream
hint.text: Upstream is against the flow of the river, towards the source.

feedback.end: The red arrow on a compass always points north. In this case, it is also pointing to the source of the river!

atoms.a: “We can see mountains in the same direction. What do you think the source will be?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>We can see mountains in the same direction, what do you think the source will be</voice>

feedback.end: Exactly! The most likely source of a river in tall mountains is snow and ice melting.

atoms.a: The River Nile is the shortest river in Africa.
A source is where a river begins.
Some rivers begin with water from a natural spring.
